**About the role**
------------------

Delivery Performance is building AI agents that support delivery teams, including agents that help write Epics and Features to the required quality standard and agents that help teams prepare for stage gates. Each agent is only as valuable as the way people actually use it. This role provides continuous user research across these agents, so the team always knows how people use them, where they struggle, whether the agents improve the work they are meant to support, and what should change.

  

Success in this role means agent owners make decisions about their agents from evidence of real use, and can see whether the changes they made have worked.

  

You will work with the Delivery Management System team, Delivery Leads, Programme and Project Managers, and the squads who use the agents day to day.

**What you’ll be doing**
------------------------

**Research planning**

* Agree with each agent owner, before every round of research, the question the round needs to answer and the decision it will inform.
* Decide where research time is spent based on where the biggest unknowns and risks are, so effort goes where it is most needed and is not spread evenly across agents.
  

**Continuous user research**

* Plan and run a continuous cycle of usability testing across every live and upcoming agent, so that each agent is tested with the people who use it on a regular rhythm and not only at launch.
* Before a new agent is built, study how teams do that work today, so the agent is designed around how the work is done.
* Find out whether each agent improves the work it supports, for example whether Epics and Features meet the quality standard and whether teams arrive at stage gates prepared, as well as whether people find it easy to use.
* Test with users across CFUs, so that findings do not rest on one group alone.
* Include people who tried an agent and stopped using it, and people who have not started, as well as regular users.
* Repeat the same tasks with users after a change has been made, and report whether the behaviour observed has changed.
* When shared on Wayfinder, are users able to find the information.
* Work with the Designer on discoverability of the Delivery Standards published including the agents and other guidelines.
  

**Observation and research practice**

* Observe people using the agents in their real work, and record what they did separately from what they said they did.
* Invite agent owners to watch sessions and to take part in making sense of what was seen, so the people who act on the findings have seen the evidence themselves.
* Support demonstrations and user sessions run by colleagues and show them how to observe without leading the user.
* Insight and recommendations
* Write up a report covering what was observed, what it means, how strong the evidence is, and a ranked set of recommendations. Agent owners decide what to act on and make the changes.
* Maintain record of findings across all agents, so that patterns and recurring needs across agents are visible.
  

**Data protection, consent and research ethics**

* Handle research data in line with BT data protection, consent and regulatory requirements, including participant privacy.
* Make sure research findings are never used to judge an individual’s performance, and tell participants this before each session.

**Essential Skills / Experience**
---------------------------------

* Strong observation skill: you can describe a session so that someone who was not there understands what happened and why it matters.
* Experience planning and running moderated usability sessions and interviews from start to finish.
* Experience agreeing research questions with stakeholders and choosing the method that fits each question, including saying when a question does not need new research.
* Experience studying how people work before a product is designed, as well as testing products already in use.
* Experience turning observations into clear recommendations, written in plain language for senior stakeholders.
* Experience researching with enterprise users within data protection and compliance constraints.
* Three or more years of experience as a user researcher.

**Desirable Skills / Experience**
---------------------------------

* Experience testing AI assistants, copilots or other AI-enabled workflow tools.
* Experience involving product owners and developers in observing sessions and analysing findings.
* Familiarity with Jira, Confluence and SharePoint as used by delivery teams.

BT Group is the UK’s leading communications group and the holding company behind some of the country’s most recognised brands – including BT, EE, Openreach and Plusnet. Our purpose is as simple as it is ambitious: we connect for good. Our customers include consumers, small, medium and large businesses, public sector organisations and other communications providers.

BT Group’s role is about setting direction, unlocking value and creating the conditions for our brands and businesses to thrive.

Having come through the most capital-intensive phase of our fibre investment, our focus now is on what comes next – simplifying how we operate, using technology and AI to work smarter, and organising ourselves to serve customers better and grow sustainably. Group teams shape strategy, policy, brand, capital allocation and transformation, helping the whole organisation perform at its best.

We have a singular culture that unites all our people: we are customer-first challengers, who are committed, clear and connected. These behaviours unite us as one team to deliver for our colleagues, our customers, our stakeholders and the country. Joining BT Group means working at the heart of a business that matters to the UK, with the opportunity to shape decisions, influence outcomes and help set the future course of one of the country’s most important companies.
